scope: frame-loop encoder overruns (82 bits) - the 5-bit value is a FIELD DISTANCE, not an absolute index

measurement.note: 1390 > 1376 (the body length) so the ps block overran the buffer

corrected_model_0x670FF0.0x671023: read 5 bits -> value V (bits from bsr(24): 5)
corrected_model_0x670FF0.0x671070: for each index strictly between old and esi: call 0x670D30 = COPY (no bits)
corrected_model_0x670FF0.0x6710AD: decode the field at index esi via 0x6701D0 (bits read here)

reading: the 5-bit value is not an absolute field index; it advances the decoder position (a field distance)
fields skipped by the advance are COPY-only (0x670D30 reads no bits), so only the landing field costs bits
that explains the 82-bit overrun: with V=8 the decoder landed near index 7 and decoded many fields, each reading bits, until it ran past the buffer
next: encode the advance as V so that the landing index is the field we want (e.g. V=9 to land on index 8, the first origin component)
then supply only that field's codec bits (positive width 10 = 1 zero-flag + 10 bits)
expect ps consumption = 1+1+5 (header) + 1 (present) + 1 (continuation) + 5 (V) + distance bits + 1 + 10 + 1 (exit) and verify against the actors entry bit
